subject: Next steps for Solaria Health procurement & payment method decision
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@solariahealth.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@solariahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps for Solaria Health procurement & payment method decision

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the pilot procurement path: 

- Recap: Solaria wants a 3-month pilot (up to 25k tokens/day) to evaluate latency and cost for patient-facing summaries.
- Primary constraints: AP requires vendor onboarding + purchase order for any commitment > $10k per quarter. For smaller/one-time items card payment is acceptable.
- Marketplace interest: Priya mentioned a preference for billing via your internal marketplace if available, but procurement would need marketplace vendor listing and tax docs.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I attached a one-page SOW and our standard pricing sheet for the pilot — can you confirm which path (PO vs corporate card vs marketplace) procurement prefers? (See attached files.)
2) If PO is required, please send the vendor setup form or procurement contact so we can complete supplier onboarding — we can return vendor docs + W9 within 48 hours.
3) If marketplace is viable, Karthik will confirm marketplace SKU + billing integration details.

Can you please reply with: (a) preferred payment route, and (b) approximate procurement timeline (vendor onboarding SLA)?

I’ll loop in our finance ops for vendor setup once you confirm.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Sheet_Q2_2027.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@solariahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@solariahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for Solaria Health procurement & payment method decision

Stephanie — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from procurement side: 

- Our AP policy requires a formal vendor onboarding and a signed PO for any vendor where anticipated spend exceeds $10k per quarter. That applies to the pilot as described if we expect to exceed that threshold.
- For engagements under that threshold or one-off purchases, we can process using the corporate card.
- Marketplace billing is ideal, but the marketplace team needs vendor listing + tax/tin docs and it usually takes 7-10 business days to approve.

Action items from our side:
1) I can get you the vendor setup form (I’ll attach in a follow-up) — we’ll need a signed W-9, address, and primary contact.
2) Our procurement lead is Sarah Kim (sarah.kim@solariahealth.com) — feel free to copy her on the vendor onboarding email to speed things up.

If Redwood can accept a short-term card payment for the initial month while we complete vendor setup, that would speed enablement. Otherwise we’ll move to PO and I’ll flag expedited processing if needed.

Best,
Daniel Park
Sr. Procurement Manager, Solaria Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@solariahealth.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for Solaria Health procurement & payment method decision

Thanks Daniel — that makes sense. Two quick notes from Redwood ops: 

- We can absolutely accept a corporate card for the initial month. If the pilot scales above $10k in a quarter, we’ll switch to a PO. We’ll provide monthly invoices and can pro-rate the first month if helpful.
- Marketplace: we have an AWS Marketplace listing and a GCP Marketplace listing (if Solaria prefers cloud marketplace billing we can surface the SKU you’d purchase). Marketplace onboarding can be parallelized with vendor setup but does require listing approval on your end.

I’ve attached a short vendor-info packet that includes our tax info and sample PO terms — this should speed Sarah up when she receives it.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) Stephanie to share vendor packet and attach our W-9 (attached).
2) Daniel to send vendor setup form or Sarah’s preferred onboarding link.
3) If card-first is acceptable, Stephanie to send a card-only invoice for month one; finance will record it and we’ll switch to PO for month two if needed.

We’ll be ready to go on our side once we have the vendor form or confirmation to invoice the card.

—Karthik
Attachment: Solaria_vendor-setup-questions.docx (DOCX)
Attachment: Redwood_Tax_W9.pdf (PDF)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>

Perfect — thanks Daniel + Karthik. Quick internal note for our tracker:

- Status: Waiting on Solaria vendor setup form (Daniel) — card-first accepted for month one.
- Owner: Stephanie to send card-only invoice and W-9 today; Karthik to provide marketplace SKU if needed.
- Ask: Marissa, can you prepare a one-line summary for finance ops (billing code, pilot SKU, expected monthly spend) so they can create the invoice? I’ll copy Sarah once we have the vendor form.

I’ll follow up once Sarah/Katie confirm the vendor setup link.

Thanks team,
Stephanie
